label: first copy-phase step after <DEL> when the fed-back first token is r
explanation: Fires only at the step right after <DEL> (recall_idx == 1), when the input is the fed-back first original token and that token is r. It is silent during the original phase, at the delimiter, and at every later copy step. About 99% of activation mass is on in_tok = r, with typical activation around 2-4 (max 4.0). The strongest examples are L = 5-6. With L = 3 it is weak or silent, and all the false positives are L = 3. There is a faint low-magnitude tail (under ~0.1 of max) at the same step when the first token is 3, x, h or l; these are about 13% of active steps but under 1% of mass. It does not depend on the token being output or on later tokens.

issues: Every factual claim held up on dev and test. All activation mass is in the copy phase. Activation is exactly zero in the original phase, at <DEL>, and at every recall_idx other than 1. in_tok = r carries 0.991 of the mass. Max activation is 4.02 and the median is 2.4.
On test, (recall_idx == 1) & (in_tok == r) scores P 0.986, R 0.866, F1 0.922 and mass recall 0.991, matching the reported numbers.

Restricting to L == 3 gives precision 0.47 on 432 steps. All 227 test false positives are L = 3 sequences at step 4, e.g. 'r c r <DEL> *r*'. This matches the claim that the feature is weak or silent at L = 3. Adding L >= 4 gives precision 1.0 and recall 0.855, so F1 is essentially unchanged.

The 2549 missed activations hold only 0.9% of the mass. They are all at recall_idx 1 with in_tok 3, x, h or l, at relative activation 0.00-0.08 of max. Each of those tokens scores precision of 0.06 or less as a predicate at that step, so they are a faint tail rather than a second meaningful trigger. This is what the explanation already says.
Minor point: recall by count is 0.866 because of that low-magnitude tail. The lowest activation quartile has only 0.46 coverage. This is acceptable given the mass recall of 0.991.
